To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a novel deep learning based model to predict the binding affinity of a given protein ligand complex.
we develop a novel, data driven deep learning model that is capable of predicting protein ligand binding affinity from the atomic coordinates of a crystal structure.
we develop and test an end to end deep learning approach to structure based bio activity prediction and show that it is comparable with state of the arts methods.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of deep learning models that are tailored to the specific requirements of drug discovery applications.
the development and application of deep learning methods to problems in drug discovery and molecular design.
the application of deep learning techniques to the problem of predicting the binding affinity of small molecules to proteins, given the 3D structure of the protein-ligand complex.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

we have developed a general 3D convolution operation that is capable of directly learning atomic level chemical interaction from atomic coordinates and demonstrated its application to structure-based bioactivity prediction.
we have developed a new deep learning based model for structure based bioactivity that is fully differentiable and end to end and that performs competitively with state of the are approaches.
atomic convolutional network is an end to end, fully differentiable, data driven model for structure based bioactivity predictions and represents a new paradigm for physics based deep learning.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we developed a new machine learning model that learns the interaction between protein and ligand from the crystal structure of protein-ligand complex and predicts the binding affinity of the complex.
we have developed an end to end deep learning model for predicting binding affinity of a ligand to protein.
we have developed a new deep learning model for predicting protein ligand binding affinity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the atomic convolutional neural networks are able to identify non covalent interactions that are absent in both the protein and ligand and are present in the complex.
the spatial arrangement of atoms is a rich source of information and that deep learning can be used to learn from this information.
the underlying physics of the system can be learned from data.
